failure_chain_review.r1: The run fatals before an end receipt while all six covers are nonzero; this is consistent with the disclosed active-region termination sampling race.
failure_chain_review.r2: The receipt is generated=2093, written=2201, read=2200 and then fatal, directly exposing the repeated-payload driver defect.
failure_chain_review.r3: The simulator reaches generated/written/read=2200/2200/2200, prints zero-mismatch PASS, and the run is nevertheless marked failed; this is consistent with the old runner matching the normal watchdog=3525 counter.
failure_chain_review.r4: RTL and SVA remain hash-identical across r1-r4; r3 and r4 TB hashes are identical. The current r4 runner narrows the regex to literal 'watchdog timeout', and a fresh exact replay passes. Thus r4 is runner-only relative to r3.
failure_chain_review.independent_limit: Failed r1-r3 runs do not retain their historical runner sources, and r1/r2 historical TB bytes are not present. The logs and frozen contract hashes support the chain, but a complete historical byte diff is impossible.

m311r4_vcs.stall_count_note: 786 is the TB count of stalled output cycles; 579 is the SVA count of stall-to-ready cover transitions. They are different observables, not a mismatch.

findings.observation: M314 meets the synthesis report numerically, but setup slack is only 0.0005 ns (0.5 ps) after 135 logic levels; hold margin is also only 0.0024 ns. Both are measured with an ideal clock, ZeroWireload and no physical SRAM or parasitics.
findings.impact: The 3 ns/333 MHz point is too fragile for physical or paper-PPA admission. Small clock-tree, routing, OCV or SRAM-boundary effects can erase the margin.
findings.required_fix: Pipeline or restructure the 16-way Hamming/min tree, then rerun exact-SHA DC and PT/physical STA with propagated clock, extracted parasitics and the target center SRAM interface; otherwise relax the target period and report the logic-only point honestly.

findings.observation: The r1-r3 failed directories preserve logs and generic failure markers but not their historical runner sources; r1/r2 historical TB bytes are represented only by contract hashes.
findings.impact: The disclosed failure chain is internally consistent and r4 replays, but an independent reviewer cannot reconstruct a byte-level r3-to-r4 runner-only diff or replay the exact r1/r2 TBs.
findings.required_fix: For future failed runs, seal runner, TB, contract, compile command and input manifest even when the run exits nonzero.

findings.observation: The native DC report proves only that max fanout does not exceed 32. The independently extracted value 29 is connected-object count minus one because fanout_number is absent from the DDC.
findings.impact: 29 is useful corroboration but should not be presented as a native DC max-fanout metric.
findings.required_fix: Emit a synthesis-time per-net fanout report or preserve a native load-pin query in the production DC flow; retain the official <=32 statement until then.

admitted: Exact-SHA M311 matcher RTL semantics in fresh VCS: Hamming nearest of sixteen centers, minimum packed unsigned center tie break, population-below-two guard, tau0 exact-only, tau1 distance-zero/one, stall stability and zero numeric/order mismatch over 2200 generated/accepted/retired transactions
Single-entry elastic matcher boundary can accept one transaction per cycle when downstream remains ready
M314 TSMC28 logic-only synthesis facts: 1965.977999 um2 standard-cell area, 2481 leaf cells, 48 sequential cells, zero macros, and no reported violations under the frozen ideal-clock/ZeroWireload SDC
not_admitted: 3 ns physical timing or 333 MHz post-route operation
Physical 256-bit center SRAM, its bandwidth, ports, area or energy
Complete PWP Conv or network integration
SAIF power, energy or paper-ready PPA
DATE comparison, headline or best-paper claim
